facts.one_liner: Sand tinted pink by fragments of red coral, inside Komodo National Park.
facts.why_go: Pink Beach in Komodo National Park owes its colour to tiny fragments of red organisms mixed with white sand. The surrounding reef is excellent for snorkelling, and Komodo dragons live on nearby islands.
facts.how_to_get_there: Boat trips from Labuan Bajo on Flores.
facts.good_to_know: Park fees apply; go with licensed guides.

facts.one_liner: Kilometres of powdery white sand on Okinawa’s Miyako Island.
facts.why_go: Yonaha Maehama on Miyakojima stretches for about seven kilometres of fine white sand and pale turquoise water, often called one of Japan’s best beaches. The Kurima Bridge leads across to Kurima Island nearby.
facts.best_time: April–October for swimming; avoid peak typhoon months.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Miyako Airport; the beach is about 15 minutes’ drive.

facts.one_liner: Turquoise water and dhow sails at the northern tip of Zanzibar.
facts.why_go: Nungwi, at the northern tip of Zanzibar, is a beach village where tides are less extreme than elsewhere on the island, making swimming possible all day. Traditional dhows are built on the beach and sunset cruises are popular.
facts.best_time: June–October and December–February for dry seasons.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 1 hour’s drive from Zanzibar Airport or Stone Town.

facts.one_liner: A long white beach on Kenya’s south coast, sheltered by a coral reef.
facts.why_go: Diani Beach south of Mombasa is a long stretch of white sand on the Indian Ocean, protected by an offshore coral reef. Colobus monkeys live in the coastal forest nearby, and kitesurfing and diving are popular.
facts.best_time: December–March and July–October for dry weather.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Ukunda airstrip or Mombasa, then about 1 hour by road and ferry.
facts.good_to_know: Look for ‘colobridges’—rope bridges built for monkeys.

facts.one_liner: Four sheltered coves between granite boulders below Lion’s Head.
facts.why_go: Clifton’s four beaches in Cape Town are separated by granite boulders and sheltered from the summer wind. With Lion’s Head behind and the Atlantic in front, they are among the city’s most fashionable beaches.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 10 minutes from central Cape Town; MyCiTi buses stop nearby.

facts.one_liner: Pine-fringed limestone cliffs around a turquoise cove on Menorca’s south coast.
facts.why_go: Cala Mitjana on Menorca’s south coast is a small, undeveloped cove of fine sand and turquoise water framed by pine-topped limestone cliffs. It is reached by a short walk from Cala Galdana.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 15 minutes’ walk from Cala Galdana; buses from Ferreries.
facts.good_to_know: Arrive early for parking and space.

facts.one_liner: A secluded pebble cove under green cliffs on the Asturian coast.
facts.why_go: Playa del Silencio near Cudillero in Asturias is a quiet, wild cove of grey pebbles beneath high cliffs and rock islets. Its peaceful beauty gives it its name.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 15 minutes’ drive from Cudillero; a footpath leads down from the parking area.
facts.good_to_know: Swimming can be rough—check the sea.

facts.one_liner: A secluded white-sand cove of turquoise water on Praslin.
facts.why_go: Anse Georgette on Praslin is one of the Seychelles’ most beautiful beaches: white sand, granite boulders and clear water framed by lush vegetation. It is reached through the grounds of the Constance Lémuria resort.
facts.best_time: April–May and October–November for calm seas.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 15 minutes’ drive from Praslin airport.
facts.good_to_know: Non-guests must request access at the resort entrance in advance.

facts.one_liner: A sheltered rock-pool bay in Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park.
facts.why_go: Shell Beach in Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park on South Australia’s Yorke Peninsula is a small, sheltered bay of white sand, clear water and rock pools. The park’s rugged coast is also home to emus and kangaroos.

facts.one_liner: A quiet palm-lined beach in South Goa, nesting ground for olive ridley turtles.
facts.why_go: Agonda is one of South Goa’s quieter beaches, a long sweep of sand backed by palms and beach huts. It is a nesting site for olive ridley sea turtles.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 1.5 hours from Goa’s Dabolim Airport.
